qs.q: A 60-year-old man with von Hippel-Lindau disease undergoes abdominal imaging. In addition to renal cysts and CNS haemangioblastomas, what percentage of patients with this specific genetic syndrome develop a phaeochromocytoma?
qs.e: Von Hippel-Lindau disease is associated with phaeochromocytomas in 10 to 20% of cases. A 50% incidence is more characteristic of phaeochromocytoma in MEN 2A, while NF1 has a prevalence of under 5%.

qs.q: A pathologist examines a lesion from a patient with von Hippel-Lindau disease. Which of the following is a characteristic vascular lesion associated with this syndrome?
o: Cavernous hemangioma of the cerebellum or retina
Glomus tumour of the distal digit
qs.e: Von Hippel-Lindau disease is associated with vascular lesions (hemangioblastomas/hemangiomas) in the cerebellum, brain stem, retina, pancreas, and liver. The other options are not specific to VHL.
